author: Clay Reporter
title: Clay County Sheriff's Office opens new $8 million law enforcement resource center
text:
Will Akin, Sheriff at Clay County Sheriff's Office | Clay County Sheriff's Office
Will Akin, Sheriff at Clay County Sheriff's Office | Clay County Sheriff's Office
The Clay County Sheriff’s Office has officially opened its new Law Enforcement Resource Center in Kearney, Missouri. The grand opening event took place on November 25 and included tours for county employees, local elected officials, and representatives from other law enforcement agencies. On the evening prior to the event, more than 40 nearby residents were given an early look at the facility.
The new center is located at 16414 N.E. 116th St. and includes a 10-lane indoor shooting range, a classroom with capacity for up to 64 people, as well as areas designed for defensive tactics and decision-making training. The facility will also offer virtual and augmented reality training opportunities. According to the Sheriff’s Office, these resources are intended to help staff meet training requirements necessary to serve Clay County’s growing population.
Funding for the $8 million project came from federal grants such as the American Rescue Plan Act and the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant. Piper-Wind Architects, Inc., served as architect on the project, while Straub Construction was the general contractor.
This marks the first major construction effort by the Sheriff’s Office since expanding the Clay County Detention Center in 2000.
"The Law Enforcement Resource Center features a 10-lane indoor shooting range, a classroom for up to 64 people, and spaces for training in defensive tactics and decision-making. It also will incorporate virtual and augmented reality training," according to information provided by the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.
